segments: Eighth Jubilee.
Kings of the Romans.
[... and] Cleopatra, queen of Egypt.
And Augustus went against him and defeated him.
And after the intercession of the Senate, Augustus was reconciled with Antoninus [Mark Antony].
Cleopatra, however, asked Antoninus for dominion over the kingdom of the Jews and of the Arabs,
and he granted it to her.
And for this reason Augustus took offense,
and went again against Antoninus and defeated him.
And he subdued Egypt again,
and captured both sons of Cleopatra who were called Helios and Selene (the Sun and the Moon),
and killed them.
Then Cleopatra and Antoninus killed themselves.
Thus the kingdom of the Ptolemies, that is, of the Greeks, also ceased from Egypt,
and all Egypt, together with all Syria, came under the dominion of the Romans.
After Cleopatra, Augustus Caesar.
When he became king over Egypt, he was named Sebastos.
And Sextilis also (the month) was named Augustus.
And in the eighteenth year of Augustus, he sent Tiberius, the general, to Armenia and subdued it.
And Herod built Samaria,
and in honor of Sebastos named it Sebastia.
And he also built the Tower of Straton,
and named it Caesarea.
And in Galilee he also built Gabala [Gaba? {OCR?}].
And in the forty-third year of Augustus,
and the thirty-third of Herod,
which is the year three hundred and nine of the Greeks [Seleucid: 309? OCR/chronology error for 309 or 311/others],
on the twenty-fifth of the First Kanun (December),
in the night dawning on Tuesday, our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was born in the flesh of the Virgin Mary, daughter of David.
And that year began on a Monday.
And in that same year, Quirinius the governor was sent by the Roman Senate,
to register the people of the Jews for the poll-tax on account of Judas the Galilean who had rebelled.
